title: No low-degree approximation of the coordinate product on the root cube
statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field and let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \neq 0$ and $\omega \neq 1$, and fix natural numbers $n, d, e, B$. Suppose that
\[
  \sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^{n}}{t}\,\abs{K}^{t} \;\le\; B
\]
and that
\[
  \abs{K}^{2^{n}} \;>\; \abs{\,\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d} \to K\,}\cdot B ,
\]
where $\abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d} \to K}$ is the number of functions from $\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d}$ to $K$. Then there is no polynomial $P \in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ of total degree at most $d$ whose bad count against the coordinate product $x \mapsto \prod_{i} x_i$ on the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^{n}$ is at most $e$; that is, every such $P$ disagrees with $\prod_i x_i$ at more than $e$ points of $\{1,\omega\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: strict counting inequality $|K|^{2^n} > |\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor+d}\to K|\cdot B$
conclusion combines total degree $\le d$ with bad count $\le e$
replaced:
Let $K$ be finite, $\omega \ne 0$, $\omega \ne 1$.  Suppose
$\sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^n}{t}\,\abs{K}^{\,t} \le B$ and
\[
\abs{K}^{2^n} \;>\; \abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + d} \to K}\cdot B .
\]
Then no polynomial $P$ with $\deg P \le d$ approximates the product
$x \mapsto \prod_i x_i$ on the root cube with at most $e$ errors, i.e. there is no such
$P$ with $\texttt{ACP.rootCubeBadCount}\ (\prod_i x_i)\ P \le e$.
